title: URL
body:
*Uniform Resource Locator* — the full address of a resource. Every part is read by a different machine:

`https://www.example.com:443/products/search?query=shoes&page=2#reviews`

- `https` — the **scheme**. Read by your browser, which decides TLS behaviour and the default port before any network call happens.
- `www.example.com` — the **host**. Resolved to an [[IP Address]] by [[DNS]], and re-read by the server as the `Host` header, since one server usually answers for many domains.
- `:443` — the **port**. Read by your machine's TCP stack. Defaults to 80 for http and 443 for https, so it's normally omitted.
- `/products/search` — the **path**. Read by the server's router to pick a handler.
- `?query=shoes&page=2` — the [[Query String]]. Sent to and read by the server, and visible in server logs.
- `#reviews` — the **fragment**. Read by your machine *only* — the browser strips it before sending, so it never reaches the server at all.

That last point is the one that gets asked in interviews.
